ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The new TV screens have the sides $16: 9$ and the old ones have the sides 4:3.
<image1>
We have a DVD that occupies exactly all the screen 16:9. We want to watch this film on the old 4:3 screen. If the width of the film occupies exactly the width of the old screen, then the empty part of the screen is:

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The new TV screens have side ratio $16:9$ and the old ones have side ratio $4:3$. A DVD fills a $16:9$ screen exactly. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the widescreen image on the left is completely filled by the DVD content; the old screen on the right is narrower and taller, and the DVD content is displayed according to the full width of the screen, with the movie area in the middle and blank horizontal bars above and below. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the old 4:3 screen width as 4 and height as 3. The aspect ratio of the DVD movie is 16:9. When the movie width is scaled to equal the old screen width 4, the movie height is 4×9/16=9/4. The old screen height is 3, so the total vertical height not occupied by the movie is 3−9/4=3/4, corresponding to the upper and lower blank bands in the figure. Blank area = width 4 × total blank height 3/4 = 3; old screen total area = 4×3=12. Therefore, the fraction of the old screen area occupied by the blank area is 3/12=1/4.

method.method_draft: Choose convenient dimensions for the old 4:3 screen, for example width 4 and height 3. From the text, the film has aspect ratio 16:9 and is scaled so its width equals the old screen width 4. Therefore its displayed height is 4·(9/16)=9/4. The old screen height is 3, so the unused vertical height is 3−9/4=3/4, split into the top and bottom bands shown in the image. Empty area is 4·(3/4)=3, while total old screen area is 4·3=12, so the empty fraction is 3/12=1/4.

method.method_draft: Compare height-per-width ratios rather than assigning dimensions. For a 16:9 film, the displayed height is 9/16 of its width. For a 4:3 old screen, the screen height is 3/4 of the same width. Since the widths match, the occupied fraction of the old screen area equals the ratio of these heights: (9/16)/(3/4)=3/4. Therefore the unoccupied fraction is 1−3/4=1/4.
method.CoT_raw:
先看图像：图中左边是更宽的 16:9 屏幕，右边是 4:3 的旧屏幕，右图上下有黑边，表示影片宽度与旧屏幕宽度相同但高度更小。
再推理：因为影片是 16:9，所以在同样宽度下，影片高度与宽度的比是 9/16。旧屏幕是 4:3，所以旧屏幕高度与宽度的比是 3/4。
题目说影片宽度正好等于旧屏幕宽度，因此比较面积只需比较高度占比。影片占旧屏幕面积的比例为 (9/16) ÷ (3/4) = (9/16) × (4/3) = 3/4。
所以旧屏幕空白面积占比 = 1 - 3/4 = 1/4。
